title: Curry
text:
Mustard seeds
Onion
Garlic
Ginger (small diced piece)
Green chili
Ground cumin
Garam masala
Curry powder
Ground coriander
Turmeric
Salt
Tomato diced (1 medium)
Yellow split peas (1 cup)
Chicken-style stock (2.5 cup)





Pressure cookerStovetop



Cook mustard seeds until sputter. Add onion, garlic, chilli, and ginger. Brown.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, cumin, salt, curry powder, garam masala. Heat through.
Add dal and stock.
Cook 10 mins on high pressure. Naturally release pressure.




Cook mustard seeds until sputter. Add onion, garlic, chilli, and ginger. Brown.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, cumin, salt, curry powder, garam masala. Heat through.
Add dal and stock (use ~3.5 cups stock, as more liquid boils off).
Bring to a boil, then simmer covered ~40–45 mins, stirring occasionally, until the split peas break down. Top up with water if it gets too thick.








Adapted from: Urvashi Pitre 2020, Pressure Cooker Rice and Dal | Toor Dal and Rice, https://twosleevers.com/pressure-cooker-rice-and-dal/
Inspired by: The Student Kitchen (2016), Herron Books

title: Curry
text:
Brinjal (Eggplant) curry






Ingredients

Mustard seeds
Brown onion
Garlic
Ginger
1 medium eggplant (cut into chunks and salted)
Tinned tomatoes (1 tin)
Tomato paste (~2 Tbsp)
Chilli
Soy sauce
Miso paste
Coconut cream (50 mL)
Vegan beef stock (1/2 cup)
Cardamom
Paprika
Garam masala
Cloves
Pepper
Cayenne pepper
Cumin
Salt
Coriander powder
Lemon
Sugar (optional)



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Fry mustard seeds in oil. Start to brown onions. Once onions start to brown add eggplant. Once brown add garlic, ginger and chilli and cook quickly. Add spices.
Add in tinned tomatoes and herbs. Add soy sauce, miso paste and coconut milk. Add vegetable or vegan beef stock.
Pressure cook for 20 mins on high pressure. Allow to naturally pressure release.




Fry mustard seeds in oil. Start to brown onions. Once onions start to brown add eggplant. Once brown add garlic, ginger and chilli and cook quickly. Add spices.
Add in tinned tomatoes and herbs. Add soy sauce, miso paste and coconut milk. Add vegetable or vegan beef stock.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently ~40 mins until the eggplant is meltingly soft, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it dries out.






Source

Adapted from: https://www.recipetineats.com/eggplant-curry-south-indian/

title: Curry
text:
Butter Jackfruit (vegan butter chicken)






Ingredients

Oil
Margarine
Cumin **
Paprika ***
Cardamom *
Curry Powder *
Cayenne pepper *
Coriander ground *
Cloves
Fenugreek leaves
Turmeric **
Garam masala **
Cinnamon (stick or ground)
Star anise
Salt
Onion
Ginger
Garlic
Chilli
Jackfruit (1 0.5L tin)
1 cup vegan chicken stock
Soy sauce
Miso paste
Sugar (optional)
Lemon
Coconut cream (200-400 mL)

Note: * s indicates relative amount (* a little, ** some, *** plenty).


Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Add oil and margarine and allow to melt. Once melted, add spices and stir to combine. Then add onion and cook for a while (~10 mins). Add garlic, ginger and chilli for a couple of minutes.
Add jackfruit and coat in spice mix. Then add stock and soy sauce and allow to boil off fluid, stirring occasionally.
Add lemon, stir and taste. If necessary, add sugar. Pressure cook for 10 mins.
Allow to naturally release pressure. Turn on sauté mode and allow additional fluid to cook off so that desired consistency is reached. While this is happening, add coconut cream and extra oil to taste.




Add oil and margarine and allow to melt. Once melted, add spices and stir to combine. Then add onion and cook for a while (~10 mins). Add garlic, ginger and chilli for a couple of minutes.
Add jackfruit and coat in spice mix. Then add stock and soy sauce.
Add lemon, stir and taste. If necessary, add sugar. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently ~25–30 mins, stirring occasionally, until the jackfruit is tender and easily pulled apart.
Uncover and let extra fluid cook off until the desired consistency is reached. While this is happening, add coconut cream and extra oil to taste.






Source

Inspired by: https://www.reddit.com/r/Cooking/comments/axmknw/ultimate_restaurant_quality_butter_chicken/
Inspired by: https://plantbasednews.org/veganrecipes/dinner/butter-jackfruit/
Inspired by: https://www.goodto.com/recipes/gordon-ramsay-s-butter-chicken



Notes

Other (better?) recipes also use cashews. It might be worth testing these.
Can replace jackfruit with tofu.

This sauce is relatively chunky compared to restaurant butter chickens. To overcome this, I think the tomato can be added before the jackfruit and that sauce blended.

title: Curry
text:
Ethiopian bean curry


Ingredients

Oil
Onion
Ginger
Chili
Garlic
Cumin
Paprika
Cardamom
Clove
Ground coriander
Turmeric
Cinnamon
All spice
Pepper
Soy sauce
Stock
Chopped tomatoes
Margarine (2 Tbsp)
Red lentils (1/3 cups)
Green lentils (1/3 cups)
Red kidney beans (x2 cans)
Wine/lemon



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Brown onions. Add ginger and chilli and brown. Add garlic and brown.
Add spices and cook until fragrant. Add stock, soy sauce, wine and chopped tomatoes. Add margarine and oil (50 mL) and wait for margarine to melt. Cook until wine starts to boil off. Pressure cook for 20 mins on high.
Add lentils and 2 cups water. Pressure cook for 15 mins on high.
Add beans. Cook on low pressure for 5 mins.




Brown onions. Add ginger and chilli and brown. Add garlic and brown.
Add spices and cook until fragrant. Add stock, soy sauce, wine and chopped tomatoes. Add margarine and oil (50 mL) and wait for margarine to melt. Cook until wine starts to boil off, then simmer covered ~15 mins to build the base.
Add lentils and 2 cups water. Simmer covered ~30–40 mins, stirring occasionally and topping up water, until the lentils are soft.
Add beans and simmer a further ~10 mins until heated through and the stew is thick.






Notes
Replacing the lemon with wine may add more depth.

title: Curry
text:
Misir Wot


Ingredients

Onion
Garlic
Ginger
Chili
Berbere (~2 Tbsp)
Cloves
Cardamom
Cumin
Cinnamon
Paprika
Nutmeg
Coriander
Turmeric
Tomato paste (~2 Tbsp)
Margarine / oil
Red lentils (1 cup)
Salt
Water or vegan stock (~3 cups)



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Dry-fry the onion (no oil) on a low heat until soft and starting to colour, stirring so it doesn’t catch. Add margarine/oil and let it melt in.
Add garlic, ginger and chilli and cook briefly. Add berbere and the rest of the spices and cook until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the rinsed red lentils and stir to coat. Add water/stock and salt.
Pressure cook for 8–10 mins on high, then naturally release.




Dry-fry the onion (no oil) on a low heat until soft and starting to colour, stirring so it doesn’t catch. Add margarine/oil and let it melt in.
Add garlic, ginger and chilli and cook briefly. Add berbere and the rest of the spices and cook until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the rinsed red lentils and stir to coat. Add water/stock and salt.
Simmer covered ~30–40 mins, stirring occasionally and topping up water, until the lentils break down into a thick stew.






Notes

Should end up thick and spoonable, not soupy. Cook off extra liquid on sauté mode if needed.

title: Pasta
text:

Add spices and herbs. Add butter and wine. Allow butter to melt.

Boil off excess fluid.




Brown onion. Add garlic. Add tofu and begin to brown. Add tomato. Stir and add stock.

Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently ~45 mins, stirring occasionally, until rich and thickened. Top up with a little water if it dries out.
Uncover and boil off any excess fluid.








I normally just use an Italian herb blend instead of the fresh herbs now
* denotes an optional ingredient





Adapted from: Aunty Louise’s recipe

title: Pasta
text:
Eggplant and black bean pasta






Ingredients

Butter
Eggplant
Salt
Onion
Garlic
Tomato cans (2x 400g)
Black beans (small can)
White wine
Olives



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Add butter to cooker on sauté. Allow to melt and add eggplant and salt. Allow eggplant to soften. Once soft add onion and allow to brown. Once brown add garlic for ~1 min. Add tomato cans and beans.
Pressure cook on high pressure for 10 mins.
Release manually. Add olives and 100 mL of olive oil. Pressure cook for another 10 mins.
Cook pasta while allowing to naturally release pressure.




Add butter to a pot on medium heat. Allow to melt and add eggplant and salt. Allow eggplant to soften. Once soft add onion and allow to brown. Once brown add garlic for ~1 min. Add tomato cans and beans.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook ~20 mins, stirring occasionally.
Add olives and 100 mL of olive oil. Simmer uncovered a further ~15 mins until the eggplant is soft and the sauce is thick.
Cook pasta and stir through the sauce.






Sources

Adapted from: Salt Fat Acid Heat’s (Samin Nosrat) Pasta alla Pomarola (p. 292)
Adapted from: Delicious Recipies for you Pressure Cooker and Slow Cooker’s (Women’s weekly) Eggplant, olive and Pine Nut Pasta Sauce



Notes
Replace butter with olive oil for a vegan version.

title: Pasta
text:
Lentil ragu






Ingredients

2 onions
5 garlic cloves
mushrooms (300g)
Carrot
Celery
4 tomatoes
Butter/margarine (100g)
4 Tbsp tomato paste
Miso paste
Soy sauce
Italian herbs
Paprika
Cumin powder
Cinnamon
Nutmeg
Black pepper
5 spice
1/2 cup wine
1 cup beef stock (strong)
100 mL oat milk
1/2 cup pearl barley
1/2 cup brown/green lentils
1 cup red lentils



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



In a food processor, finely chop onion and garlic, then mushrooms, then carrot/celery, then tomatoes.
Brown onion and garlic in oil. Then add butter, some salt and mushrooms. Brown and wait for smell to change. Add carrot and tomatoes and wait for fluid to largely boil off.
Add tomato paste, miso paste, soy sauce, herbs/spices (use relatively sparingly), wine, beef stock and milk. Cook until thickened has largely boiled off.
Pressure cook for 20 Mins on high. Release pressure manually.
Add pearl barley and 2 cups of water. Cook on high pressure for 10 mins (increase to 15 mins for less chewy pearl barley). Release pressure manually, noting warnings about releasing manually when cooking with pearl barley.
Add lentils and 3.5 cups of water. Cook on high pressure for 15 mins.




In a food processor, finely chop onion and garlic, then mushrooms, then carrot/celery, then tomatoes.
Brown onion and garlic in oil. Then add butter, some salt and mushrooms. Brown and wait for smell to change. Add carrot and tomatoes and wait for fluid to largely boil off.
Add tomato paste, miso paste, soy sauce, herbs/spices (use relatively sparingly), wine, beef stock and milk. Cook until thickened has largely boiled off.
Simmer covered ~30 mins to develop the base, stirring occasionally.
Add pearl barley and 2 cups of water. Simmer covered ~30–40 mins until the barley is tender, topping up water as needed.
Add lentils and 3.5 cups of water. Simmer ~25–30 mins until the lentils are soft, stirring occasionally so it doesn’t catch.






Sources

Inspired by: The ultimate traybake ragu, Y. Ottolenghi and I. Belfrage 2020, Flavour, Ebury Press. This recipe is clearly a traybake ragu and is clearly very different. The ingredients are very similar but the method is pretty much completely different.



Notes

The cooking times are currently indicative. The first pressure cook is optional, but is partly intended to break down the veges. It can be increased/decreased depending on how chopped the veges are (increase if they are less chopped).
Spices should be used reasonably sparingly and are largely optional (pepper and paprika seem to be good though). I’m still not sure which set of spices are optimal

title: Pasta
text:
Broccoli cream pasta






Ingredients

Onions
Broccoli
Asparagus (optional)
Garlic
Cream (300 g)
Butter
Parmesan cheese



Steps

Brown onion and Broccoli until the broccoli becomes soft. If using asparagus add this. Add garlic and quickly brown.
Add in cream and cook until desired consistency reached (~20 mins). Add a small amount of butter (~50g).
Add in pasta and parmesan.



Sources

Adapted from: Salt Fat Acid Heat’s (Samin Nosrat) Pasta with broccoli and bread crumbs and Pasta cacio e pepe

beans (3x cans)
tofu (200g)
Eggplant, finely chopped and salted
Onion
garlic
chilli
garlic

Paprika >>>

Cinnamon >

All spice >
Salt >>
Pepper >>
Coriander (ground) >>

bread 2 slices torn into small pieces
Puff pastry

Key: > a little (~1/2 tsp), >> some (1 tsp), >>> plenty (~3 tsp)




Brown finely chopped onion. Then add garlic, chilli and ginger until aromatic. Add spices and soy sauce and wait for smell to change.
Add eggplant and \(\approx 1\) cup water, allow to soften. Then add tofu and cook until spice begins to absorb.
Separately, mince beans (e.g. with a fork) until forms a smoothish paste, with some chunks remaining.
Stir the beans into the tofu/eggplant mix. Add bread.
Put mix into pastry and bake on \(180^oC\) until brown.












Base mix (see below)
Italian herbs >>>
Paprika >>>
Cumin >>
Cayenne Pepper >
Cinnamon >
Cardamom (ground) >
Salt >>
Pepper >>
Curry powder >
Coriander (ground) >>
Oil
bread 2 slices torn into small pieces
Puff pastry
Almond milk
Sesame seeds





Use one portion of base mix. Add herbs, spices and bread and mix together. Add oil and stir thoroughly.
Put mince onto pastry and roll. Top with almond milk and sesame seeds Cook in oven at 200C for 25 mins (time will depend on oven heat and roll size).













eggplant
onion
garlic
oil
beans (2x cans)





Slice eggplant and rub with salt. Wait 20 mins.
Finely dice eggplant, onion and garlic.
Brown onion, then add eggplant and allow to soften. Then add garlic.
Mince beans into a smoothish paste. Add to the onion/eggplant mixture. Add additional oil if required.













Mushrooms (200g)
Eggplant
Onion
Garlic
Chilli
Oil
Butter





Slice eggplant and rub with salt. Wait 30 mins.
In separate batches, blend mushrooms, eggplant, onion, garlic and chilli in a blender.
Brown onion in oil. Add butter and salt, once melted add mushrooms and allow to brown.
Make space in pan, add more oil if needed and add garlic and chilli. Stir in side of pan until ready then mix into remaining mixture.

title: Mexican
text:
Onion
Garlic
Chilli (small with seeds)
Tofu
Beef stock
Cumin
Cayenne pepper
Paprika
Salt
Coriander
Miso paste
Oregano
Black beans
Beer (Australian lager) (<1/2 cup)
Lime juice (1/2 lime)
Butter (50g) or olive oil
1 dessert spoon corn flour





Pressure cookerStovetop



Soak ground tofu in 1/2 cup of strong beef-style stock.
Brown onion in oil. Add garlic and chilli.
Add spices and salt. Cook for a while.
Add tofu and miso paste. Cook until stock/water begins to boil off.
Add Black beans, beer and lime juice. Boil off much of the remaining fluid. Stir and let settle. Add corn flour.
Add butter or additional oil. Stir in.
Pressure cook 20 mins (TBC).

title: Mexican
text:
Chilli






Ingredients

Onion
Garlic
Red + green chilli
Capsicum
Cumin powder
Cayenne pepper
Coriander
Oregano
Paprika
Cinnamon
Brown sugar
Salt
Miso paste
Soy sauce
1 star anise
cocoa powder
brown sugar (1 large tsp)
Butter
Tomato diced (2 cans)
Tomato paste
Tofu (1 packet)
Beef stock (1/2 cup)
Beer (1/2 cup)
Beans (2 cans; black + kidney)



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Brown onion, garlic, and chilli. Add in capsicum.
Add spices/herbs to taste.
Add tofu, tomato, beer, miso, soy sauce, sugar and stock. Stir until heated. Add butter and allow to melt.
Cook on high pressure for 20 minutes. Allow to naturally release pressure ~10 min.
Taste and add spices as required. Add beans and cook for another 10 mins.
Naturally release pressure. Brown to remove any extra liquid.




Brown onion, garlic, and chilli. Add in capsicum.
Add spices/herbs to taste.
Add tofu, tomato, beer, miso, soy sauce, sugar and stock. Stir until heated. Add butter and allow to melt.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook ~40 mins, stirring occasionally.
Taste and add spices as required. Add beans and simmer a further ~15 mins.
Uncover and reduce to remove any extra liquid.

title: Mexican
text:
Mexican-style rice






Ingredients

Onion
Garlic
Chilli
Peas + corn
Oregano
Cumin
Cinnamon
Paprika
Salt
Pepper
Tomato paste
Tomato
Lemon
Beans (red and kidney)
Rice (1 cup)
Chicken stock (1.5 cups)



Steps

Pressure cookerStovetop



Brown onion. Add garlic and chilli. Then add peas + corn.
Add spices and stir until aromatic.
Add tomato, tomato paste, lemon, beans, rice and chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Pressure cook for 4 minutes.




Brown onion. Add garlic and chilli. Then add peas + corn.
Add spices and stir until aromatic.
Add tomato, tomato paste, lemon, beans, rice and chicken stock (use ~2 cups liquid for the stovetop). Stir to combine.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to low, cover, and cook ~18–20 mins until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Rest covered 5 mins, then fluff.

title: Mexican
text:
Guacamole






Ingredients

Onion
Chilli
Coriander
Salt
Tomato
Avocado
Cumin (1/2 teaspoon, max)
Lime juice



Steps

Mince onion, chilli, coriander and salt together, ideally with a mortar and pestle
Add to a bowl with tomatoes, additional onion, 1/4 of the avocado, and cumin. Mix together into a reasonably consistent mix.
Add remaining avocado so that it remains chunky. You may want to use different avocado chunk sizes.
Add lime juice.

title: Other
text:
Olive oil
Margarine*
Mushroom (~250g)
Eggplant (salted)
Onion
Garlic
Wine (1/2 cup)
Olives
Frozen peas
Italian herbs
Soy sauce (2 tsp)
Miso paste
Risotto rice (1.5 cups)
Vegan chicken stock (3 cups)





Pressure cookerStovetop



Cook mushrooms in oil and/or margarine and salt until it begins to soften. Add eggplant and allow this to soften. Then add onion. Then make space in the pan, add more oil and quickly cook garlic in this.
Add in rice and allow to toast. While cooking, add in pepper, italian herbs, miso paste and soy sauce.
Add in wine and allow to partially cook off. While cooking off, add peas and olives. Once cooked off add stock.

Lentil Soup






Ingredients

Oil
Carrot
Onion
Celery
Garlic
Green Chilli
Wine
250g Lentils
400g Canned, crushed tomatoes
1L Stock (Chicken)
Parsley/italian herbs
Pepper
Paprika
Salt
Pepper
Cinnamon*
Fennel*
Cloves*
Margarine*
Soy sauce*
Miso paste*
Liquid smoke*
Nutritional yeast*



Steps

In a large pot, heat butter and oil over medium heat. Add diced onion, celery, and carrot. Sauté until the onion turns transparent and the vegetables soften, about 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Add minced garlic and chopped green chili to the pot. Sauté briefly, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, allowing it to simmer until most of it has evaporated, stirring occasionally. This step enhances the flavor of the soup.
Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, parsley or Italian herbs, and selected spices. Optionally, add a modest amount of miso paste and soy sauce for depth of flavor.
Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover the pot. Allow the soup to simmer for approximately 1 hour, adjusting the cooking time to achieve your preferred level of tenderness for the lentils. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.




Notes
* Denotes optional ingredient

title: Other
text:
Falafel






Ingredients

Core Ingredients:

Chickpeas: 2 cups, dried, soaked overnight
Brown Onion or Shallots
Garlic: 4–6 cloves
Fresh Parsley: 1/2-1 cup
Fresh Cilantro: 1 cup
Paprika
Cumin
Ground Coriander
Salt
Black Pepper
Baking Powder: 1/2 tsp
Sesame Seeds
Water: As needed, a tablespoon at a time, to add moisture if the mixture feels too dry.



Optional Add-ins:

Mint
Lemon Zest
Chili: 1/2 large red chillies
Fresh Ginger: one small piece
Turmeric
Sunflower Seeds





Instructions

Preparing the Mixture

Soak the Chickpeas
Place dried chickpeas in a large bowl and cover with plenty of water. Soak overnight (8–12 hours) until they are plump and softened. Drain and allow to dry.
Blend the Ingredients
In a food processor, combine the soaked chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cilantro, and all spices. Pulse the mixture in short bursts until it has a coarse, grainy texture. It should hold together when pressed but not turn into a paste. Avoid over-blending.
Add Sesame Seeds and Adjust Consistency
Stir in sesame seeds. If the mixture feels too dry, add water one tablespoon at a time. If it’s too wet or loose, refrigerate to firm it up. Optionally, add a small amount of chickpea flour or breadcrumbs for extra binding.
Chill the Mixture
Transfer the falafel mixture to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and make shaping easier.




Frying Instructions

Prepare the Oil
Heat vegetable, canola, or sunflower oil in a deep skillet or pot to 180–190°C. Use a thermometer for accuracy.
Shape the Falafel
Scoop about 2 tablespoons of the chilled mixture and shape it into balls or small patties. Work quickly to prevent the mixture from warming up.
Test the Oil
Drop a small piece of the falafel mixture into the oil. If it sizzles without burning, the oil is ready.
Fry the Falafel
Gently lower falafel balls or patties into the hot oil. Fry each side until golden brown and crispy.
Drain the Falafel
Remove the falafel from the oil and transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.

Smoky Eggplant, Tofu & Mushroom Dumpling Filling (vegetarian)






Ingredients

Oil

Onion (1, minced)

Garlic

Ginger

½ long fresh chili

Carrot (1 small, grated)

Mushrooms (1 cup, ~300 g, finely chopped)

Eggplant (450 g, steamed until soft)

Tofu (300 g, firm, crumbled)

Soy sauce **

Miso paste **

Shaoxing wine *

Liquid smoke *

Smoked paprika **

Turmeric *

Salt & pepper **



Steps

Steam eggplant until soft, set aside.

Heat oil, sauté onion until soft. Add garlic, ginger, chili; cook briefly.

Add carrot, mushrooms, tofu. Stir-fry until moisture cooks off.

Deglaze with wine, add soy sauce, miso, liquid smoke, paprika, turmeric. Stir to combine.

Add eggplant, mash in, season with salt & pepper. Cook until thick.

Cool before filling dumplings.

Kidney beans



Dried red kidney beans contain a toxin (phytohaemagglutinin) if undercooked. Cooking them from dry through to fully soft in the pressure cooker destroys it — just don’t stop them short of done, and don’t cook them only in a low-heat slow cooker.
